names.usage: The oldest and universal form of the divine name. Used alone or as a prefix/suffix in other names (El-Shaddai, Elohim). Transcends Semitic cultures.
Most common name in the OT. Grammatical plural used with a singular verb — sign of fullness and majesty. Some see it as a prefiguration of the Trinity. Used as early as Genesis 1:1.

names.meaning: I AM WHO I AM / The Eternal
names.usage: God's own name, revealed to Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3:14). Sacred Tetagram — Jews do not pronounce it and say 'Adonai' instead. It is the name of the Alliance, of presence and fidelity.
Title of absolute sovereignty. Used in place of YHWH in the synagogue reading. Expresses God's total lordship over all creation and His people.

Name revealed to Abraham. 'Shaddai' probably comes from 'shad' (breast) — nourishing and sufficient God, or from 'shadad' (destroy) — Almighty God. Both meanings coexist: absolute strength and maternal care.
Name used by Melchizedek (Genesis 14:18). Expresses the absolute transcendence of God above all gods and all authority. Used in contexts of victory and sovereignty.
Name revealed in Beersheba. 'Olam' = eternity, permanence. God whose nature transcends time and whose promises never end. Abraham plants a tamarisk tree to celebrate this name.
Name given by Hagar in the desert (Genesis 16). The only name for God given by a woman in the Bible. Expresses that God sees the suffering of the forgotten and excluded.
Expresses God's exclusive and passionate love for his people — like a husband jealous of the exclusivity of married love. It's not jealousy-envy but jealousy-fidelity.
Revealed to Abraham on Mount Moriah, after God provides a ram to replace Isaac. This name establishes the doctrine of divine providence: God sees in advance and provides.
Revealed after the victory over Amalek. Moses raises his hands and Israel wins. The altar built is called 'The Lord is my standard' — a sign that God himself is the standard under which we fight.
Revealed to Gideon, who feared he would die after seeing the angel of the Lord. Name of an altar built in Ophrah. Shalom = wholeness, prosperity, harmony, absence of internal war.

The most beloved name of the Hebrew people. Psalm 23 — David expresses the relationship of total trust with God as shepherd: direction, nourishment, protection, presence in death. Jesus appropriated the title (John 10).
Name of the military and celestial power of God. 'Tzabaot' = armies (armies of Israel + heavenly armies). Reveals that God is the commander-in-chief of the forces of heaven and earth.
Revealed to Marah, after God makes bitter waters sweet. God reveals himself as a healer of his people—physically (diseases) and spiritually (wounds of the heart and of sin).
Last name revealed in the OT, by Ezekiel to designate the restored Jerusalem. The presence of God is the ultimate definition of the perfect city. Foreshadows the New Jerusalem (Revelation 21:3).

Messianic name revealed by Jeremiah to designate the future king of the line of David. This king (the Messiah) will himself be the righteousness of God for his people—foreshadowing justification by faith.
Revealed in the context of the Sabbath law. God does not just justify — he sanctifies, sets apart, makes holy. The Sabbath is the sign of this continued sanctification.

names.meaning: The Mighty, the Bull of Jacob
names.usage: Title used in Jacob's blessings. 'Avir' = strong as a bull. Expresses the raw power of God as protector and defender of his people.

Title dear to the prophet Isaiah (25 occurrences in his book). Expresses the absolute holiness of God — his radical otherness, his purity, his moral integrity. Holiness is the central attribute of Isaiah 6.
Hebrew legal term for the close relative who redeems an impoverished family member. Applied to God: he redeems Israel from slavery and repairs what was lost. Ruth and Boaz illustrate this concept.
God is presented as king of Israel and the universe. Central title in the royal Psalms (93, 96-99). The OT theocracy is based on this title: God himself is the true king.

Title of filial intimacy, developed in prayer. Rare in the OT (Isaiah 63:16), it expresses the relationship of paternal tenderness. Jesus will make it the main name in the Lord's Prayer ('Our Father').

pronunciationNote: The sacred Tetagram (יהוה - YHWH) is never pronounced in Jewish tradition out of respect for divine holiness. The synagogue readers say “Adonai” in his place. The vocalization “Jehovah” is a medieval combination of the consonants of YHWH and the vowels of Adonai.
